candidates.rule: Do not re-query DatasetDagRunQueue (or any table already loaded into memory) inside the per-DAG scheduler loop; pass already-fetched data through instead to avoid N+1 queries.
candidates.trigger: A new session.scalars() or session.execute() call targeting DatasetDagRunQueue appears inside a for-loop that iterates over dags_needing_dagruns or dataset_triggered_dag_info.

candidates.rule: When eager-loading is absent on a SQLAlchemy relationship used inside the scheduler loop, do not access that relationship attribute lazily; either add eager loading or pass the data from the outer query.
candidates.trigger: A scheduler-loop function accesses a dotted relationship attribute (e.g. record.dataset.uri) on a model where the relationship is not declared with lazy='joined' or joinedload().

candidates.rule: Every locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ must declare that it extends the global rules in ../SKILL.md, and must state that the locale file takes precedence over global rules on any conflict.
candidates.trigger: A new or modified locale skill file (.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/<lang>.md) does not contain a reference to ../SKILL.md and a precedence statement.

candidates.rule: In locale do-not-translate lists, mark only the bare Airflow noun (e.g. 'Asset') as untranslatable; do not block compound phrases (e.g. 'Asset Events') when existing translations already translate the surrounding words.
candidates.trigger: A locale skill file's do-not-translate list includes a multi-word phrase containing an Airflow term (e.g. 'Asset Events', 'Dag Run') when the existing locale JSON files translate the non-Airflow words in that phrase.

candidates.rule: Docs for extensible Airflow interfaces (state backends, secrets backends, etc.) must describe the contract and behaviour rather than listing concrete method signatures, which are subject to change.
candidates.trigger: A .rst documentation file adds a list-table or code-block containing full method signatures (async def ...) for a pluggable backend or extension point interface.

candidates.rule: CI shell scripts that start 'airflow standalone' in a polling loop must check process liveness with 'kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID' to exit early when the process crashes instead of looping for the full timeout duration.
candidates.trigger: A CI shell script starts airflow standalone in the background, captures its PID, and then polls in a timed loop without a kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID liveness check.

candidates.rule: AIP skill SKILL.md files must anchor the AIP URL pattern to the Apache Confluence prefix (https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW) rather than a generic https:// host.
candidates.trigger: A SKILL.md under .github/skills/aip-* describes AIP URL detection as 'Other https:// arguments are the AIP URL' without anchoring to the cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW prefix.

candidates.rule: Locale skill files must cross-reference the rationale documented in the corresponding airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<lang>/README.md when consolidating translation conventions.
candidates.trigger: A locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ is created or updated without a reference to the in-tree i18n README for that locale.

candidates.rule: Each upload-artifact step in a GitHub Actions workflow must use a unique artifact name; never reuse the same name (including names that share a dynamic suffix) across multiple upload steps in the same job.
candidates.trigger: Two or more actions/upload-artifact steps within the same job share the same `name:` value or the same name template (e.g. both use container-logs-${{env.JOB_ID}}).

candidates.rule: Do not include unrelated uv.lock churn in a feature or fix PR; either revert lock-file changes or split them into a separate commit with a stated reason tied to the PR.
candidates.trigger: uv.lock appears in the diff of a PR whose description does not mention a dependency bump, and the lock diff is larger than a few lines.

candidates.rule: Task-SDK client changelog entries must appear in the Task-SDK changelog, not in the core airflow-core RELEASE_NOTES.rst.
candidates.trigger: RELEASE_NOTES.rst receives a line mentioning 'task-sdk', 'task SDK', or 'Task SDK client' in a section that belongs to airflow-core.

candidates.rule: A database migration included in a patch release must only repair a bug in an existing migration; it must not change payload semantics so that users who already ran the original upgrade end up in a different state from a fresh installer.
candidates.trigger: A patch-release PR modifies a file under migrations/ (or alembic/versions/) and the diff touches both upgrade() and downgrade() logic beyond simple no-op corrections.

candidates.rule: Any new config option introduced in a patch release must be declared in config.yml and explicitly documented in the relevant upgrade notes for that minor version.
candidates.trigger: A patch PR adds a new key to config.yml or references a new [section] key_name in documentation without a corresponding entry in the upgrade notes.

candidates.rule: A reusable workflow that has a committer allowlist on workflow_dispatch must apply the same allowlist check to its workflow_call trigger so that callers cannot bypass the gate.
candidates.trigger: A workflow file defines a committer-restricted workflow_dispatch block but also exposes a workflow_call trigger without an equivalent contains(fromJSON([...]), github.event.sender.login) guard.

candidates.rule: Provider policy documentation must not imply that a sponsoring committer is absolved of technical responsibility for PRs they merge; committers retain responsibility for CI health and security review regardless of steward approval.
candidates.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst (or equivalent governance doc) contains a sentence stating the sponsor is NOT responsible for the codebase or for merged PRs.

candidates.rule: Use vendor-neutral examples (e.g. the http provider) rather than named commercial vendors when illustrating provider policy concepts in governance documentation.
candidates.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or a provider governance document uses a specific vendor name (e.g. Slack, AWS, GCP) as the sole illustrative example of a policy concept.

candidates.rule: Docs code examples must use the correct Airflow API method name; use `.partition_key_pattern()` for regex filtering, not `.partition_key()` (exact-match).
candidates.trigger: diff adds a docs example calling `.partition_key(` with a regex string argument

candidates.rule: When documenting a new Airflow feature that was introduced in a specific version, give it a dedicated `.. note::` block or subheader rather than nesting it under an existing section that covers a different feature.
candidates.trigger: diff adds documentation for a new feature (e.g. Resumable Tasks) inside an existing section that already documents a distinct feature (e.g. Deferred Operators)

candidates.rule: In newsfragments and release notes, capitalise "Dags" (title-case), not "DAGs" (all-caps).
candidates.trigger: diff in a newsfragment file contains the word "DAGs" (all-caps)

candidates.rule: Significant newsfragments about permission or endpoint changes must explicitly name the surface (e.g. "FastAPI UI `/dags` endpoint") to distinguish it from other endpoints with the same path.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `significant.rst` newsfragment mentioning a `/dags` or other ambiguous endpoint without specifying whether it is the FastAPI UI route or a public REST API endpoint

candidates.rule: Do not enable asyncio debug logging in production code paths or default configuration; it can expose credentials in task logs.
candidates.trigger: diff enables `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG`, `loop.set_debug(True)`, or asyncio debug logging in non-test production code

candidates.rule: Do not add native/binary C-extension libraries as mandatory dependencies of `airflow-core`; they must be optional extras or provider-level dependencies.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a native library (e.g. one distributed as a compiled wheel with no pure-Python fallback) to the `dependencies` list in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml`

candidates.rule: In `BaseAuthManager` and its subclasses, `is_authorized_*` methods must accept `user: T` (the generic auth-user type-var) and represent multiple user IDs as `set[str]`; they must not accept concrete Airflow model types (e.g. `HITLUser`) as parameters.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or modifies an `is_authorized_*` method on an auth manager class that takes a concrete Airflow model type (e.g. `HITLUser`, `DagModel`) instead of `user: T` or primitive types

candidates.rule: Derive `TASK_SDK_VERSION` from `PACKAGE_VERSION` using `packaging.version.parse_version()` (accessing `.minor` and `.micro`), never by splitting the version string on `.`.
candidates.trigger: diff introduces `PACKAGE_VERSION.split('.')` to derive TASK_SDK_VERSION or any component version

candidates.rule: Auth manager docs must reference `get_url_refresh()` for the token-refresh endpoint path, not a hardcoded literal path such as `POST /auth/token/refresh`.
candidates.trigger: diff hardcodes an auth token refresh URL path in documentation instead of referencing the `get_url_refresh` method

candidates.rule: Airflow docs must describe the current state of a feature without comparing to a previous version; do not use phrases like "no longer", "previously", or "as of version X".
candidates.trigger: diff adds text containing "no longer", "previously", "used to", or "as of Airflow X.Y" in documentation prose

candidates.rule: Document task-state-store and asset-state-store values as `JsonValue` (JSON-serialisable types), not as plain strings.
candidates.trigger: diff documents task store or asset store value types as "string" or "str" rather than `JsonValue` or JSON

candidates.rule: Public consumers of `XCOM_RETURN_KEY` (and other XCom constants) must import from the Task SDK's `BaseXCom`, not from `airflow.models.xcom`.
candidates.trigger: diff imports `XCOM_RETURN_KEY` or other XCom constants from `airflow.models.xcom` in user-facing code or docs

candidates.rule: Docs about authentication must not present the FAB Auth Manager as the default; the default auth manager in Airflow 3 is the Simple Auth Manager.
candidates.trigger: diff adds documentation or configuration examples that imply FAB Auth Manager is used by default

candidates.rule: Getting-started / quickstart docs must document both the `uv`-based install path and the standard `pip` + `venv` path, not only one.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or rewrites the Airflow install quickstart section covering only a single tool (`uv` only or `pip` only)

candidates.rule: Use a `bugfix.rst` newsfragment (not `significant.rst`) for non-user-facing internal fixes; omit the fragment entirely if the fix has no observable user impact.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `significant.rst` newsfragment for an internal race-condition fix or scheduler-internal improvement with no API/behaviour change

candidates.rule: Extend an existing `is_authorized_*` method with an optional parameter rather than adding a parallel `is_authorized_*_for_<entity>` method to the `BaseAuthManager` interface.
candidates.trigger: new method added to BaseAuthManager whose name matches `is_authorized_.*_for_` pattern

candidates.rule: Do not set `document.title` dynamically inside React components for Airflow UI pages; the global title is already defined in `index.html`.
candidates.trigger: `document.title` assignment inside a `useEffect` hook in a `.tsx` file under the Airflow UI source tree

candidates.rule: When silently coercing an unrecognised stored value to `None` in a Pydantic validator (e.g. for `asset_expression`), emit a `log.warning` so that schema drift between the server and the DB remains observable.
candidates.trigger: `except ValidationError: return None` in a Pydantic validator without a preceding `log.warning` call when `value` is not `None`

candidates.rule: Boolean timetable properties used by the API (e.g. `is_backfillable`) must be persisted in `DagModel` via a DB migration rather than derived at runtime from `timetable_summary` string matching.
candidates.trigger: a `frozenset` of timetable summary strings used in a datamodel or route to derive a boolean DAG property instead of reading a `DagModel` column

candidates.rule: When redacting a dict value (e.g. Trigger kwargs) in an API response serializer, keep it as a JSON-serialisable dict rather than wrapping it in `str()`.
candidates.trigger: `str(redact(value))` where `value` is a dict in a Pydantic response serializer or validator

candidates.rule: Compare `DagRunType` enum members directly (e.g. `DagRunType.MANUAL`) rather than their `.value` attribute when checking membership in `dm.allowed_run_types`.
candidates.trigger: `DagRunType.<member>.value not in dm.allowed_run_types` (accessing `.value` before membership test)

candidates.rule: When multiple code paths implement partition-date-window localization with different interval conventions (inclusive vs half-open), add a cross-reference comment or consolidate to avoid silent drift.
candidates.trigger: inline `timetable.localize_partition_datetime` call in a route that duplicates the logic in `DagRun.apply_partition_date_window` with a different interval boundary

candidates.rule: Validate that a requested `try_number` actually exists in the DB before using it to generate extra links; return 404 for non-existent try numbers.
candidates.trigger: `ti.try_number = try_number` assignment in an extra-links route without a preceding DB check that the try number exists

candidates.rule: Do not use the name `task_instance` for a variable that may hold either a `TaskInstance` or a `TaskInstanceHistory`; use a neutral name (`row`, `entity`, `model`) to avoid type confusion.
candidates.trigger: variable named `task_instance` assigned from a query that can return either `TI` or `TIH` ORM objects

candidates.rule: Place `_ImportPathCallbackDef` (and similar callback-definition objects) in the domain model module (e.g. `models/test_connection.py`) rather than directly in the route handler file.
candidates.trigger: `_ImportPathCallbackDef` or `ExecutorCallback` construction inlined inside a route handler function body

candidates.rule: Use `entity.name` (not `entity.pool` or other wrong attribute) when collecting pool names in bulk-action validation; verify attribute names against the actual Pydantic body class before building error lists.
candidates.trigger: `invalid_entities.append(entity.pool)` or similarly wrong attribute access on a `PoolBody` instance inside bulk-action validation

candidates.rule: Re-use `resolve_user_from_token` (in `core_api/security.py`) instead of calling `get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token` directly in middleware or route code.
candidates.trigger: direct call to `get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token(` outside of `resolve_user_from_token`

candidates.rule: Name JWT duration parameters `valid_for` (a relative duration), not `expiry` or `expires_at` (which imply an absolute timestamp).
candidates.trigger: parameter named `expiry` or `expires_at` on a JWT-generation method that actually receives a TTL integer/timedelta

candidates.rule: When cursor pagination encounters an unparseable cursor token (e.g. malformed UUID for a `Uuid` column), raise HTTP 400 rather than silently falling back to the original value.
candidates.trigger: `except (ValueError, Exception):` block inside `_coerce_value` or cursor-parsing code that returns the raw `value` instead of raising

candidates.rule: Keyset cursor pagination over nullable sort columns must use null-aware comparisons (e.g. `IS NULL` tie-break or `COALESCE`) matching the ORDER BY null-ordering semantics; bare `col > NULL` comparisons silently break paging.
candidates.trigger: cursor `or_clauses.append(and_(*eq_conditions, col > value))` where `col` can be nullable without a corresponding `IS NULL` guard

candidates.rule: Use `if/elif` (not sequential `if`) when filter parameter branches for mutually exclusive bound conditions (`lower_bound` vs `lower_bound_excluded`) to avoid emitting redundant SQL WHERE clauses.
candidates.trigger: two consecutive `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound` / `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound_excluded` blocks that should be mutually exclusive

candidates.rule: Use `SerializedDAG` (imported under `TYPE_CHECKING` from `airflow.serialization.serialized_objects`) as the concrete type annotation for DAG-bearing attributes in API parameter/datamodel classes rather than `Any`.
candidates.trigger: property or attribute typed `None | Any` in a parameter/datamodel class where the value is a serialized DAG object

candidates.rule: Queries that use `_RegexParam` must be wrapped with `apply_regex_query_timeout`; document this obligation in the `_RegexParam` docstring.
candidates.trigger: use of `_RegexParam` or `regex_param_factory` in a route without a corresponding `apply_regex_query_timeout` call, or a `_RegexParam` class/factory lacking a docstring warning about the timeout requirement

candidates.rule: In `SortParam.get_resolved_columns()`, derive `attr_name` after applying `to_replace` so that the resolved name matches the actual ORM attribute used in ORDER BY and cursor encoding.
candidates.trigger: `attr_name = lstriped_orderby` set before the `to_replace` mapping is applied in `SortParam`

candidates.rule: Cursor-paginated endpoints must fetch limit+1 rows to detect whether a next page exists, and must return next_cursor as null when no further rows exist.
candidates.trigger: A paginated endpoint returns next_cursor/previous_cursor computed from the current page slice without fetching an extra probe row.

candidates.rule: Cursor-paginated endpoints must return previous_cursor as null on the first page (no cursor supplied) and next_cursor as null on the last page; tests must assert both boundary conditions.
candidates.trigger: New cursor-pagination route added without tests asserting previous_cursor=null on page 1 and next_cursor=null on the final page.

candidates.rule: Do not add two fields with singular/plural variants of the same name to a Pydantic response model unless they have clearly distinct semantics documented on the model.
candidates.trigger: A Pydantic model gains a new field whose name is the plural (or singular) form of an existing field (e.g., partition_key and partition_keys).

candidates.rule: Fields added to the execution-API worker context model (DagRun in taskinstance.py) must be verified as actually consumed by the worker before merging.
candidates.trigger: A nullable field is added to the DagRun StrictBaseModel in execution_api/datamodels/taskinstance.py without evidence that the worker reads it.

candidates.rule: Shared helpers used by both bulk-update and bulk-delete handlers must accept the HTTP method as a parameter rather than hardcoding 'PUT', to ensure correct auth-manager decisions for DELETE actions.
candidates.trigger: A shared authorization helper (e.g., _categorize_entities) contains a hardcoded method="PUT" but is also called from a bulk-delete code path.

candidates.rule: Do not reuse the bulk-service interface for single-item state operations; use the single-item service code path instead.
candidates.trigger: A non-bulk route (e.g., PATCH task group state) instantiates a BulkService with a dummy empty BulkBody to drive a single-item update.

candidates.rule: When a new code path is introduced in a service method, verify that the serialisation layer (_serialize_response or equivalent) is also updated to include it; do not merge dead-code branches.
candidates.trigger: A new conditional query branch is added in a service method but the response-serialisation helper still gates on the old condition, leaving the new branch unreachable.

candidates.rule: The handle_bulk_delete handler must apply the same state guards as the corresponding single-delete endpoint unless the relaxed behavior is explicitly documented and intentional.
candidates.trigger: handle_bulk_delete is added or modified without a guard matching the single-delete state check (e.g., refusing RUNNING DagRuns).

candidates.rule: When constructing a large dict to pass to Model.model_validate(), assign the dict to a named variable first, then call model_validate() on the next line.
candidates.trigger: Model.model_validate({...}) is called with a multi-key inline dict literal containing computed or conditional expressions.

candidates.rule: Do not use getattr(Model, 'field') in SQLAlchemy column-selection expressions; resolve optional or dynamically-named columns inside the model definition instead.
candidates.trigger: A SQLAlchemy select() call uses getattr(SomeModel, 'column_name') to reference a column.

candidates.rule: conf.getboolean() calls for feature-flag config keys must not supply fallback=False when the config default is True; doing so silently overrides the configured value and breaks the UI toggle.
candidates.trigger: conf.getboolean(section, key, fallback=False) is used in a UI config endpoint for a key whose intended default is True.

candidates.rule: New default behavior changes to public endpoints (e.g., /dagRuns/{run_id}/wait) must be covered by tests asserting the new default, results-absent, and authorization scenarios.
candidates.trigger: A service method changes what an endpoint returns by default (e.g., now includes dag_result XComs when result param is omitted) without updating existing tests.

candidates.rule: PATCH routes that honour update_mask must raise HTTP 422 when a field is included in update_mask but its value is null/None in the request body.
candidates.trigger: A PATCH handler checks fields_to_update/update_mask but does not validate that each included field has a non-null value before passing data downstream.

candidates.rule: New validation branches in bulk-operation endpoints must be covered by tests asserting the new HTTP 400 response.
candidates.trigger: A bulk endpoint gains a new validation guard (e.g., multi_team check) without corresponding test cases for the 400 path.

candidates.rule: Do not introduce CASE-based NULL ordering in query ORDER BY clauses; rely on database-default NULL ordering to keep indexes usable.
candidates.trigger: A SQLAlchemy query adds a CASE expression in its ORDER BY to place NULLs last/first.

candidates.rule: Grid-endpoint queries must select columns explicitly rather than using select(Model); never select the whole ORM model.
candidates.trigger: A query on the grid endpoint uses select(TaskInstance) or select(DagRun) instead of enumerating required columns.

candidates.rule: Parallel subquery predicates (e.g., has_note, has_missed_deadline) must use the same filter conditions across DagRun and TaskInstance counterparts.
candidates.trigger: A subquery EXISTS predicate on DagRunNote or TaskInstanceNote differs in filtering conditions (e.g., .isnot(None)) between the DagRun and TI versions.

candidates.rule: Every new endpoint registered in the execution API's authenticated_router must have a matching endpoint(...).didnt_exist entry in the unreleased Cadwyn version file.
candidates.trigger: A new router is added to authenticated_router.include_router() in airflow-core/src/airflow/api_fastapi/execution_api/routes/__init__.py without a corresponding didnt_exist entry in versions/v*.py.

candidates.rule: Query-string regex parameters must reject empty-string values with HTTP 400; do not silently execute regexp_match("").
candidates.trigger: A query parameter intended as a regex pattern (e.g., partition_key_pattern) is validated only against None, not against the empty string "".

candidates.rule: When AssetActive rows are removed during GC, decide and implement a strategy to handle orphaned asset_state rows; do not leave them to accumulate forever.
candidates.trigger: A new asset_state table/model is introduced without a cascade-delete from AssetActive removal or a GC policy.

candidates.rule: Use `session.flush()` instead of `session.commit()` within multi-operation task-completion workflows to preserve transaction atomicity; an early `commit()` inside `register_asset_change` leaves `AssetEvent` persisted even if a subsequent operation rolls back, creating inconsistent state between task state and asset events.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or changes `session.commit()` inside `register_asset_change` or any method that is called as part of a task-completion transaction spanning multiple models

candidates.rule: When early visibility of an `AssetEvent` is required before the caller's transaction commits, use `create_session(scoped=False)` to open a truly independent session/connection rather than calling `session.commit()` on the shared session.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `create_session` call near `AssetEvent` insertion, or replaces `session.commit()` with a separate session block in `assets/manager.py`

candidates.rule: All new routers in the execution API must set `route_class=ExecutionAPIRoute`; omitting it means the `allowed_token_types` default falls back to `{"execution"}` only, silently blocking any future `token:workload` routes on that router.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a new `VersionedAPIRouter(...)` in `airflow-core/src/airflow/api_fastapi/execution_api/routes/` without `route_class=ExecutionAPIRoute`

candidates.rule: When `?all_map_indices=true` on a task-state endpoint can affect sibling mapped tasks (different TIs with different tokens), the route must either use a broader scope (e.g. `ti:fleet`), require a leader check (`map_index in (-1, 0)`), or document the intentional fleet-wide authority in the docstring.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an endpoint parameter (e.g. `all_map_indices: bool`) that expands the scope of a state-mutation beyond the single TI identified by the JWT subject

candidates.rule: Execution-API list endpoints that query the metadata DB must apply pagination (`limit`/`offset`) or a documented hard cap; unbounded `session.scalars(stmt).all()` on large tables (e.g. Variables) is a slow-query risk at scale.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a GET list route in the execution API that calls `session.scalars(stmt).all()` without a `limit`, `offset`, or `LIMIT` clause

candidates.rule: High-volume execution-API endpoints (e.g. heartbeat) must use `log.debug` rather than `log.info` for fall-through diagnostic messages that fire on every fast-path miss; INFO-level logging on high-frequency paths floods production logs.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `log.info(...)` on a fallback or miss path inside a heartbeat or high-frequency execution API handler

candidates.rule: When archiving a `task_instance_history` snapshot on the retry path, copy `rendered_map_index` onto the in-memory TI object whenever the field is present in the patch payload, even when its value is `None`; a `None` check silently omits the cleared value from the archive.
candidates.trigger: diff archives a TIH row and conditionally sets `ti._rendered_map_index` only when the payload value is not None (e.g. `if ti_patch_payload.rendered_map_index is not None:`)

candidates.rule: FastAPI router path ordering in the execution API must avoid greedy path parameter matching; static path segments (e.g. HEAD routes) must be declared before parameterised routes at the same prefix level.
candidates.trigger: diff reorders or removes `@router.head(...)` declarations relative to `@router.get(...)` with overlapping path patterns in the execution API routes

candidates.rule: In `config.yml` descriptions, write `Dag` (title-case, not `DAG`) when referring to the Airflow concept in prose; use `DAG` only in code identifiers or quoted strings.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or modifies a `description:` block in `config.yml` containing the word `DAG` in a prose sentence (not inside backticks or a code identifier)

candidates.rule: config.yml descriptions must not expose internal DB table names (e.g. `task_state rows`) in user-facing text; describe the concept abstractly instead.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `description:` in `config.yml` that references an internal database table name (e.g. `task_state rows`, `dag_run rows`)

candidates.rule: Do not use `conf.has_option` to test whether a boolean config option is True or False; `has_option` returns True whenever the key exists (including when the stored value is False), producing incorrect branching for tri-state boolean configs with a `~` default.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `conf.has_option(section, key)` as a condition that branches on a boolean config option declared with `type: boolean` and `default: ~` in config.yml

candidates.rule: CLI date-range arguments that filter by a `partition_date` must document whether the end date is inclusive or exclusive and what the correct bound is for an entire calendar period (e.g. January); ambiguity between midnight-on-the-last-day and first-of-next-month causes silent data loss.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `--start-date` / `--end-date` (or similar) CLI arguments that filter DAG runs or partitioned runs by date in `cli_config.py` or `dag_command.py`

candidates.rule: When locking an `AssetModel` row with `with_row_locks`, select only the primary key column rather than the full ORM object to confine the lock to an index scan and avoid fetching the entire row.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `with_row_locks(select(AssetModel).where(...))` that retrieves the full model when only the id is subsequently used

candidates.rule: When `parsedate` returns a UTC-normalised datetime, the help text for that CLI argument must note that the calendar day is derived from the UTC instant, not the user's local timezone or the timetable's timezone; a tz-aware input can silently shift the interpreted date.
candidates.trigger: diff uses `type=parsedate` for a CLI argument whose help text says "time-of-day is ignored" but does not mention that the calendar day is the UTC calendar day of the parsed instant

candidates.rule: A PR that bundles logically independent features (e.g. DAG caching + worker recycling) must either update the PR description to explicitly include all features with rationale and compatibility notes, or split into separate PRs.
candidates.trigger: diff in `api_server_command.py` or a scheduler/worker config file introduces a second independent feature (e.g. `limit_max_requests`) alongside the one described in the PR title

candidates.rule: Duplicate post-resolution logic shared between multiple asset-store endpoints (e.g. `/by-uri/value` and `/by-name/value`) must be extracted into a helper function to ensure consistency between the two paths.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a second execution-API asset-store route whose body after the `_resolve_asset_id_by_uri` / `_resolve_asset_id_by_name` call is identical or near-identical to an existing route

candidates.rule: Do not call `session.flush()` in a `finally` block when the block is entered during an exception path; flushing inside an error handler is meaningless if the transaction will never be committed.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `session.flush()` inside a `finally:` or `except:` clause in an asset or scheduler code path

candidates.rule: The `token:workload` scope must not be granted on mutation routes (PUT/POST/DELETE); restrict `token:workload` to read-only routes (GET variable/keys, GET/HEAD xcom, GET connection, GET dag_run) and keep write/delete routes as `token:execution` only.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `Security(require_auth, scopes=["token:execution", "token:workload"])` on a router.put, router.post, or router.delete endpoint in the execution API

candidates.rule: Do not add `token:workload` as an accepted scope on endpoints that previously relied on `has_variable_access` or `has_xcom_access` guards without also restricting those endpoints to reads only; the workload token is a long-lived, low-privilege token and must not be broadened to cover state-changing operations.
